models.name: Sol
models.note: OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The only model in this map whose API accepts None effort.

models.name: Astra
models.note: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra for complex reasoning and end-to-end work. Its API effort range starts at Low.

models.name: Opus 5
models.note: Claude Opus 5. Thinking is on by default and can be disabled at High or below.

models.name: Fable 5.1
models.note: Claude Fable 5.1 for long-horizon agentic work. Adaptive thinking is always on.

openai: No reasoning effort. A separate Sol setting, not another name for Low.
Light in the ChatGPT apps: for quick, well-scoped tasks.
Balances speed and depth for tasks that need more planning.
For difficult work with multiple steps.
The higher of the two settings for difficult multi-step work. Test it against High on a specific unresolved problem.
More time for reasoning on a single task. Test whether it changes the result before keeping it.
anthropic: Fewest tokens and tool calls. Anthropic suggests lower effort once your checks show quality holds.
A balanced setting for bounded work. Keep it if your checks show quality holds.
Anthropic’s recommended starting point and the API default.
Anthropic’s setting for demanding, long-running agentic work. A candidate to test on harder tasks.
Highest effort setting for especially demanding work. Compare the result with Extra High before keeping it.

ENV.chat: ChatGPT in the browser and on my phone
ENV.review: ChatGPT desktop app, reviewing my coding agent

t1.note: Astra Light is fine if it is already selected.
t1.why: The priority is faithful capture, not unsolicited analysis.
t1.title: Dictated notes, capture, summaries

t2.why: Sol carries ordinary conversation well and keeps the conversational and editorial character I like.

up.when: when another analytical approach or stronger constraint tracking would help.

t2.title: Conversation and thinking aloud

t3.why: Medium is Astra’s broad analytical band: quality and judgment without paying for High on every question.

up.when: when important tradeoffs or contradictory evidence are being flattened.

t3.title: Comparing tools, untangling questions

t4.why: Source quality still matters more than the label.

up.when: for unusually difficult synthesis, calculations, or verification.

t4.title: Serious research and analysis

t5.why: Image concepts, Suno direction, reference analysis. Higher effort does not select a better renderer and does not guarantee taste.

up.when: one rung up on the model in use when many creative constraints interact, or repeated attempts drift.

t5.title: Art direction and reference analysis

t6.why: Locating code, explaining a function, a basic summary: a small inspection does not need the review default.

up.when: when the request becomes a substantive correctness review.

t6.title: Small diffs and explanations

t7.why: Cross-file behavior, architecture, requirements. Review is what I use the desktop app for, so Extra High is its standing default. Start with the change set; expand into dependencies only when warranted.

down.when: for a small inspection, or bounded follow-through after the review.

up.when: when one specific hard issue is still unresolved after a checked attempt. Include the failed attempt, the evidence, and the exact issue.

t7.title: Reviewing substantial changes

t8.note: With screenshots or the running interface in front of the reviewer.
t8.why: Code inspection alone cannot tell whether a design works visually.
t8.title: Visual review of an interface

t9.why: Familiar patterns and scoped fixes rarely need more.

up.when: when dependencies are unclear, reasoning is shallow, or fixes fail.

t9.title: Routine implementation

t10.why: High is the vendor’s starting point on Opus 5. Extra High is justified by the work, never a standing default.

up.when: only if the specific problem remains unresolved.

t10.title: Difficult implementation

t11.why: Many interacting requirements need the planning High buys.

down.when: for mechanical follow-through once the decisions are settled.

t11.title: Substantial features, nuanced design

t12.why: Broad dependency changes and hard bugs are where I spend Extra High: the vendor’s setting for capability-sensitive, long-horizon work.

down.when: once the problem is understood and bounded.

up.when: for one clearly defined frontier problem after a checked attempt.

t12.title: Architecture, migrations, hard debugging
